title: MCP Tasks (async): Why Aren't Any Agents Supporting Them? — Cornelia Davis, Temporal
talk_summary: Cornelia Davis explains MCP Tasks as durable async tool invocations that return handles, and why clients have avoided V1 because of stateful task-list and long-lived elicitation complexity. She shows V2 moving to a stateless core with tasks as an extension, explicit update signals, persisted task IDs, and notification-based scaling.

takeaways.technique: Durable async task handles with persisted IDs
takeaways.what_they_do: Long-running MCP tool calls return a task handle; the task must survive client/server/network/human delays, and clients must persist task IDs to reconnect.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once you've locked launched a task it has to be durable

takeaways.technique: Signal/update endpoint instead of long-lived elicitation connection
takeaways.what_they_do: V2 replaces input-required over a long-running session with a client update endpoint, so task results no longer depend on a held-open connection.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of having this input required going over a long-running session

takeaways.technique: Stateless core, async tasks as extension
takeaways.what_they_do: MCP V2 moves to a stateless core and makes tasks an extension, avoiding stateful task-list and long-lived protocol handlers.

takeaways.technique: Notification endpoint instead of per-task polling
takeaways.what_they_do: At scale, per-task GET polling from many clients does not scale; a single notification endpoint tells clients which task changed, then they pull that task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: single endpoint where they can say, "Has something changed?"

takeaways.technique: Map task lifecycle to domain state machine
takeaways.what_they_do: Server-side task lifecycle states are mapped onto the application's own domain state machine, with explicit working/input-required/completed/failed states.
takeaways.evidence_quote: mapping from the life cycle states of the task over to the domain state machine

takeaways.technique: Implement async MCP client as workflow
takeaways.what_they_do: The speaker implemented the complex MCP client protocol and elicitation handling as a workflow rather than ad hoc code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I've implemented it as a workflow
